summary: A 1979 DNR cab from Mount Spokane was set on a new 10 ft tower on Quartz Mountain in 2004 and is now a summer rental in Mount Spokane State Park.

facts.design: 10 ft tower carrying a 14x14 ft wood-frame live-in cab with wrap-around windows and deck; the cab was built in 1979 on a 40 ft tower on Mount Spokane
facts.agency: Washington State Parks, Mount Spokane State Park (cab built by Washington DNR)

access.note: Reservable rental through Washington State Parks: summer only, reservations up to nine months ahead, two-night minimum, sleeps four

visit.trail_note: Hike-in or bike-in only; the trail is 2.7 miles from parking at Selkirk Lodge

corrections.current: None relocated (Moved from Mount Spokane to Quartz Mountain.)
corrections.proposed: relocated 2004: the cab was moved off the Mount Spokane summit (removed 2001) and set on a new 10 ft tower on Quartz Mountain (2004)
corrections.why: NHLR records 'Built 1979 - Relocated 2004' and describes the move in its description; FFLOS says the tower was removed from Mt. Spokane in 2001 and placed on Quartz in 2004. The brief's 'None relocated' is wrong.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1979 is the build year for the current cab and tower (NHLR, TrailChick). TrailChick dates the start of the site's lookout history to the 1934 Vista House, while Washington State Parks gives completion as November 21, 1933. The 1948 and 1950 towers are earlier history on the same summit, not the Quartz structure.
NHLR gives 5,180 ft (1,579 m), TrailChick 5,160 ft and FFLOS 5200 ft. The record's 1578.9 m matches NHLR and was kept.
NHLR and TrailChick both give about $100 a night. Washington State Parks refers visitors to its fee page without quoting a price, so the figure is not confirmed against an official rate.
Washington State Parks gives the trail as 2.7 miles from Selkirk Lodge; TrailChick gives 2.25 miles one way. The story uses the state figure.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree the current cab dates from 1979 and moved to Quartz in 2001-2004. Brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with the state rental terms. The 'None relocated' event was wrong and is corrected. The roughly $100 nightly rate comes from NHLR and TrailChick (TrailChick last updated May 6, 2026); the state page does not quote a price, so the rate is unconfirmed. FFLOS says the cab is available for emergency detection, but no source describes current fire watch. The site's older history (1933 Vista House vs 1934 per TrailChick) is noted but not part of the cab's own record. Sources were fetched from the cache; the Mount Spokane record page referenced in the brief was not read.
